prompt: Why does the RISC-V spec reserve dedicated opcode values like custom-0 (0001011) for user-defined instructions instead of extending into an existing opcode such as OP-IMM?
choices: Custom-0/1/2/3 are permanently carved out for non-standard extensions, so they can never collide with a current or future standard extension
OP-IMM instructions cannot have a funct7 field, so new opcodes are mechanically required for any instruction with one
The RISC-V decoder hardware physically cannot route instructions with opcode 0010011 to a custom ALU operation
Custom-0 opcodes execute in fewer clock cycles than instructions under the OP-IMM opcode
